Cosmati VERSION for Windows (64-bit): Tessera as a plugin
===========================================

In this folder:
  Cosmati.clap    the CLAP instrument (use this one if your DAW has CLAP: Bitwig, Reaper, FL Studio, ...)
  Cosmati.vst3    the VST3 instrument
  Cosmati.exe     the standalone app: no DAW needed

Install
-------
1. Copy Cosmati.clap to   C:\Program Files\Common Files\CLAP\
   Copy Cosmati.vst3 to   C:\Program Files\Common Files\VST3\
   (Make the CLAP folder if it isn't there. Windows asks for an administrator's OK to copy there.)
2. In your DAW, rescan the plugins. Cosmati is an instrument, under "Rastapopolix".

Until beta 4 Cosmati was called Tessera: before step 1, delete Tessera.clap and Tessera.vst3 from
those folders (and Tessera.exe), so the DAW doesn't find it twice. Songs saved with them open in
Cosmati.

The standalone app needs no install: double-click Cosmati.exe and pick an audio output.

"Windows protected your PC"
---------------------------
This beta isn't signed, so Windows SmartScreen may warn about Cosmati.exe the first time. Click
"More info", then "Run anyway". The plugins themselves are loaded by your DAW and don't show this.

Signing takes this warning away; a Windows code-signing certificate costs money every year. If you'd
like to help get Cosmati signed: https://ko-fi.com/Rastapopolix

If Windows blocks the downloaded zip's files: right-click the zip, Properties, tick "Unblock", OK,
then unzip again.

The manual for the plugin: https://github.com/Rastapopolix/tessera/blob/main/PLUGIN.md
What's in this beta, and what isn't yet: BETA_NOTES.md in this folder.
Found a problem? https://github.com/Rastapopolix/tessera/issues (the plugin's version, your DAW and its
version, Windows' version, the steps, what you expected and what happened).
